neighbours.label: ' be' (or the auxiliary) right before an expected 'done', where the subject is unspecified action ('more needs to be', 'something had to be', 'much remains to be')
fire: The flood wrecked half the town, and everyone agrees that more needs to be done.
We fixed the roof last month, but a great deal of work remains to be done.
Prices kept falling all year, so the president decided that something had to be done.
She saw that the shelter was short of staff and did whatever needed to be done.
The report is a good start, although much more needs to be done.
Crime is rising in the city, and the mayor insists that something must be done.
The treaty is signed, but plenty of work still needs to be done before it takes effect.
The doctors told the family that nothing further could be done for him.
quiet: The flood wrecked half the town, and the old bridge needs to be replaced.
We fixed the roof last month, but the chimney remains to be painted.
Prices kept falling all year, so the president decided that he had to be firm.
She saw that the shelter was short of staff and asked to be transferred.
The report is a good start, although the last page needs to be shorter.
Crime is rising in the city, and the mayor insists that the police must be paid more.
The treaty is signed, but the annex still needs to be translated before it takes effect.
The doctors told the family that the patient could be moved on Friday.

notes: Fires before the participle, so 'be said' fires too if the frame is the same. A concrete subject ('the house has to be', 'the floor needs to be') stays near zero. The output suppresses ' perform', and the - pole is the perform/carry-out side.
